# Recovery Assertion

## H1 — Goal

Add `total(items)` to `totals.js`, returning the sum of `item.price` values, and make `app.js` print `total([{price:2},{price:3}])`. All existing tests must continue to pass.

## H2 — Handoff Revision

Governed handoff: `handoff.md` at `41b1ed11ad2f3ba785556c672aa1ea239086b65f4e8d7f079d7a6b94b93d9b88`, based on commit `a15489f3136179a6df1914217cf0f5ae2fd9e221`.

## H3 — Verified State

No work is verified. The ledger contains only initialization and preparation of round `R-01`, slice `S1`. No bound verification receipt exists.

## H4 — Unverified / In-Progress State

No governed progress is recorded. The observed slice target `totals.js` is empty. Its commit/worktree status is unverified, and this observation must not be treated as completed progress. No deterministic checks are declared for this slice.

## H5 — Pending Action

Execute only slice `S1`: implement `totals.js` so it exports `total(items)`, sums numeric `price` fields, and returns `0` for an empty array. Changes must remain within the allowed paths: `totals.js`, `app.js`, and `tests.js`.

## H6 — Blockers

There is no recorded blocker to beginning the legal slice action. The executor cannot independently advance verification or declare completion; verification requires the existing Gate to pass, an independent review to pass, and a bound receipt written by a Conductor whose identity differs from the executor.

## H7 — Legal Next Action

The next legal action is a scoped edit to `totals.js` implementing the `S1` contract. Work on another slice, scope expansion, or a completion declaration is not legal.

## H8 — Non-Goals / Forbidden Scope

There is no scope beyond the stated task. The forbidden paths are:

- `.tad/scripts/`
- `.claude/`
- `.tad/hooks/`

Hidden acceptance is outside the executor’s namespace and must not be inspected.

## S1 — Why the Next Action Is Legal

Implementing `total(items)` in `totals.js` directly fulfills the current `S1` outcome, maps to `SC-1`, uses an explicitly allowed path, and does not cross the stop condition of scope drift.

## S2 — Why Verified Work Must Not Be Redone

The execution policy forbids redoing verified work because verification is authoritative governed state. There is currently no verified work to redo; if verification later advances, that work must be preserved rather than repeated.

## S3 — Why Blind Retry / Self-Completion Is Unavailable

No failed governed attempt or retry authorization is recorded, so a blind retry has no ledger basis. Self-completion is unavailable because executor assertions, completion prose, ordinary files, checkpoints, and self-authored receipts cannot advance `verified`. Shell/Bash and agent spawning are also denied in strict Phase 2, and no deterministic checks were predeclared.

## S4 — Rejected Actions

Rejected actions include declaring the goal or slice complete; treating uncommitted observations as progress; starting another slice; redoing verified work; inspecting hidden acceptance; modifying forbidden paths; editing outside `totals.js`, `app.js`, or `tests.js`; using Shell/Bash or spawning agents; and expanding beyond the stated task.
